verdicts.detail: verified malware: Exam-proctoring evasion tool with a bundled browser-credential stealer. The newly-added bin entry (hehehe: bin/kalamasha-tool.js) copies its Electron binary to a stealth-renamed SearchFilterHost.exe so the running process masquerades as a genuine Windows Search component and survives proctoring software's process-kill sweeps, with a watchdog logging to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Diagnostics\boot.log - a path crafted to blend into the real Windows AppData tree. It also ships bin/chrome_cookies.ps1 (sha256 304cbfaa42291e2b590563a2b8a00021a1ec64e4c0a336ba3e936c34aad35370), a Chromium DPAPI cookie decryptor targeting openai.com / chatgpt.com session cookies; that component is currently DORMANT (not wired to the install hook or bin entry), which is why confidence is 0.75 rather than higher. Linked by identical publisher and a byte-identical stealer file to shadxino@2.0.8 - same actor, two names. Deliberate detection evasion plus a credential-decryption capability is the conviction basis; the electron postinstall itself is the benign ABI-probe shape.
